aperture_validity.basis: the source marks surface 6 as the aperture diaphragm, a plane with a zero spacing to surface 5 (the plane rear face of the cemented pair). The diaphragm is carried as surface 5's clear aperture (0.25 mm, a derived nominal opening) inside that element's 0.57 mm edged outline, so light outside the opening meets the element's opaque rim
aperture_validity.consequence: the opening limits the beam, so the record is eligible for stop-dependent evaluation; the engine carries the stop as that surface's clear aperture and builds no separate plate (conversion counts report aperture_stops 0)
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: eligibility only: a stop-dependent match needs evidence (a field point or pupil sample), which this batch does not assert

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 587.5618 nm (the d line: the table's index column is labelled ndj / vdj), converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact) to 587.7218645 nm
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states one index per glass at the d line. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; a single d-line index per glass does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.conditions: the publication's parameter table 1 states 'Focal length f 1.000', a value normalised to f = 1.000 rather than a length measured at the prescription's scale; the prescription's own spacings put the design at 1.00137 mm
effective_focal_length_mm.note: recorded as the source states it. A normalised 1.000 is a design target, not a measured focal length, so it is not used as a paraxial match target

back_focal_length_mm.definition: the publication states 'Back focal length Bf 2.520' together with a row labelled 'Back focal length ratio Bf/f', so the number is a length in units of f, measured from the last lens surface to the image formation position with the light-path deflecting prism in place (the patent's own definition, in its statement of what a long back focal length means). It is not measured from the prism's rear face, which is the last vertex of this Project
back_focal_length_mm.note: with f = 1.000 mm the value is 2.520 mm. The conversion's air-equivalent distance from the last lens surface (surface 11) to the paraxial focus for the stated 10 mm object is 2.5152 mm, 0.19 % short of it

total_track_mm.definition: first surface vertex to the image plane along the axis, the sum of the source's stated spacings (0.32905 + 0.28827 + 1.01476 + 0.32905 + 0.00000 + 0.02879 + 0.79760 + 0.08226 + 0.82262 + 0.32905 + 0.53487 + 3.00000)

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length
comparison.why: the source states its focal length as the normalised target 1.000 and its back focal length as a ratio to it (Bf/f), so neither is a millimetre-measured first-order value: the guide's rule excludes a normalised f = 1.000 from a MATCHED verdict. The engine's 1.001365 mm is 0.14 % above the target, far outside the 1.1e-4 mm allowance the rule would give, and the engine's -0.09321 mm back focal length is measured from the last vertex (the prism's rear face), which is not the surface the patent's Bf refers to. The engine values are recorded as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts only

engine_check.note: the engine's back focal length is the component's infinite-conjugate value from the last vertex. The design's own conjugate is finite (10.0 mm object distance): for that conjugate the same ABCD puts the paraxial focus at z = 7.55920 mm, 0.0029 mm behind the source's stated image plane at z = 7.55632 mm, and the air-equivalent distance from the last lens surface (surface 11, z = 4.02145 mm) to that focus is 2.5152 mm against the patent's stated 2.520 mm

aperture.note: the publication's parameter tables state no F-number, no entrance pupil diameter and no numerical aperture, so no system-aperture value is asserted rather than inferred

clear_semi_diameter_mm.note: the source states no clear aperture. The opening was set to 0.25 mm as a nominal endoscope pupil (about f/4.4 at the engine's 1.0014 mm focal length); it is a conversion choice, not a source value, and it changes no first-order quantity

stop_geometry.source_surface: 6 (the aperture diaphragm), carried on surface 5, the plane rear face of the cemented pair

field.definition: the publication's parameter table 1 states an 'Angle of view (degs)' of 139.7 for this example; the value is read as a full angle of view, and the half field is derived by halving it
field.basis: SOURCE_STATED (parameter table 1, column 1: Angle of view 139.7 degs)

also_stated.note: the same table also states an image height. It is recorded as stated and is not converted into or from the angle of view: with the table's own -62.2 % distortion the two describe the same field only through that distortion, which this constant-index model does not represent

field.convention_note: the source states a full angle of view and does not say whether it is measured to the 50 % or the 100 % relative-illumination point; the record keeps the stated number and derives the half field by halving it

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd; the source's vd is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour, the patent's stated lateral chromatic aberration and the -62.2 % distortion figure are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the d line only

the source states no clear apertures and no F-number. The stop opening was set to a nominal 0.25 mm (about f/4.4 at the engine's 1.0014 mm focal length); the axial marginal ray for that opening and the chief ray through the stop centre, scaled so that the paraxial image height equals the stated 1.008 mm (object height -10.518 mm at the 10.0 mm object distance), give the bundle envelope |chief| + |marginal|. Each group was given the largest bundle height inside it, rounded up: 0.62 / 0.58 mm on the front negative lens, 0.55 mm on the cemented pair before the stop, 0.35 mm on the first element after it, 0.60 / 0.62 mm on the next, 0.72 / 0.82 mm on the cemented doublet and 1.02 mm on the prism, each edged at 0.02 mm beyond the clear aperture. The front aperture is capped where the source's own radii would otherwise make surfaces 2 and 3 intersect (surface 2 has R 0.6996, so its clear aperture is 0.58 mm), which vignettes the paraxial extreme field: the source's -62.2 % barrel distortion means the real field bundle is much smaller than the paraxial one. Semi-diameters set the stop plate and the solid checks, not the first-order values

the source's surface 5 is a plane with a zero spacing to the aperture diaphragm (surface 6). Surface 5 is not a dummy plane: it is the plane rear face of the cemented pair (glass before it, air after it), so it is kept and the diaphragm is carried as that surface's clear aperture, with the diaphragm's own 0.02879 mm spacing becoming surface 5's thickness. No source surface is lost, no surface is added and no optical path is changed; the conversion counts report aperture_stops 0 because the stop is not a member of its own

the source's last surface (12) carries 3.0 mm of glass (nd 1.51633), the light-path deflecting prism the patent's text describes, and the image formation surface lies at its rear face, so the image space of the source table is glass. The format requires an air image space, so the rear face is entered as surface 13 with zero spacing to the image plane. It is the same physical surface, not an added element, and it adds no optical path

the source's parameter table 1 states an object distance of 10 (mm) for every example of the table, read as the distance from the object plane to surface 1 and entered on the OBJ row. The engine's paraxial focus for that conjugate lands at z = 7.55920 mm, 0.0029 mm behind the stated image plane at z = 7.55632 mm, which supports the reading and the table-to-prescription mapping
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

wavelength_band_nm.basis: the intersection of the valid bands of the materials used

conversion.surface_labels: the source's own surface numbers are kept as the row labels, except the stop: source surface 6 (the aperture diaphragm) is labelled STO and carried on source surface 5, which is where it physically sits (zero spacing). Rows 1-12 are the source's surfaces in order; row 13 is the rear face of the source's 3.0 mm prism, which is where the source's image formation surface lies (see PRISM_REAR_FACE_AT_IMAGE_PLANE). No source surface was removed, and the table's only zero-spacing row (surface 5) is absorbed into the stop row rather than deleted

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0
project solids reported no error-severity finding; its six findings are INFO-level edge-thickness reviews that the source's own thick elements and 3 mm prism produce, not geometry errors

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the source states its focal length as the normalised target 1.000 and its back focal length as the ratio Bf/f = 2.520, so there is no millimetre-measured first-order pair to match. The engine gives 1.001365 mm and -0.093215 mm (the latter from the last vertex, the prism's rear face, which is not the surface the patent's Bf refers to)
cross-check only, not a match: the air-equivalent distance from the last lens surface to the paraxial focus for the stated 10 mm object is 2.5152 mm against the stated 2.520 mm (0.19 % apart)

the stated object distance of 10 mm is supported by the geometry: the paraxial focus for that conjugate falls 0.0029 mm behind the source's stated image plane, so the table-to-prescription mapping used here (prescription table 1 with column 1 of parameter table 1) is consistent
the source's distortion (-62.2 %) and lateral chromatic aberration (-1.41 um) are stated by the table but are not modelled or verified by this record
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted
